info.title: Zoho Analytics API
info.description: API for Views Management in Zoho Analytics — covering view operations, auto analysis, favorites, and trash management.

tags.name: View Operations
tags.description: APIs for creating, copying, renaming, deleting, and retrieving views.

tags.name: Auto Analysis
tags.description: APIs to automatically generate a curated set of views - charts, pivot tables and summary views - from an entire table or from a single column of it. Both APIs work only on Tables, Query Tables and Pipeline Tables.

tags.name: View Preferences
tags.description: APIs to mark a view as a favorite for the authenticated user and to remove it from the favorites list. The favorite status is stored per user.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: APIs to create, update, delete and list the tags of a workspace, and to attach those tags to views. A tag is a workspace-scoped label with a name and a hex colour code, used to organise tables, reports, dashboards and other views. Tags carry no permissions - attaching one neither grants nor restricts access. The tag-side APIs attach or detach one tag across many views and require workspace administration; the view-side APIs attach or detach many tags on a single view and are also open to the view owner and to users with Edit Design permission. A view can carry at most 10 tags.

tags.name: Trash Management
tags.description: APIs to list the views available in the trash of a workspace, restore a trashed view back to the workspace, and permanently delete a view from the trash.

post.description:
Creates a copy of an existing view - a table or an analysis view - within the same workspace.

The new view is independent of the original once created; later changes to one do not affect the other. For a table, `copyWithData`, `copyWithLookup` and `copyHugeData` control how much of the source is reproduced. For an analysis view those three attributes are ignored and only the view definition is copied.

The ID of the newly created view is returned in the response and is used to reference the copy in subsequent APIs.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is a valid, accessible workspace. |
| 7104 | Source view not found. | Verify that the view-id exists within the specified workspace. |
| 7111 | A view with the given viewName already exists in this workspace. | Choose a different, unique name for the new view. |
| 7144 | The specified folderId does not exist in this workspace. | Provide a valid folder ID from within the same workspace, or omit folderId to place the view at the root level. |
| 7301 | The user does not have permission to duplicate this view. | Ensure the user is a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, Organization Admin, or holds Design and Modify permission on the workspace. For analysis views, the user must also hold save permission on the parent table. |
| 7319 | The source view does not belong to the specified workspace. | Ensure that the workspace-id and the view-id are correct and consistent. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.create scope. |

schemaOnlyCopy.description: Duplicates a table with its columns, data types, lookup references and formula definitions but without any row data, and places the copy in a specific folder.

CONFIG.viewDesc: Copy of Sales table for archival

asyncDataCopy.description: Duplicates a large table together with its row data. The copy runs asynchronously in the background so that the request returns without waiting for the data to finish populating.

analysisViewCopy.description: Duplicates a chart or other analysis view. Only viewName and viewDesc are meaningful here - the table-specific attributes are ignored for analysis views.

CONFIG.viewDesc: Duplicate of Q3 revenue trend chart

200.description: OK. The new view was created and its ID is returned.

newViewCreated.description: The ID of the newly created view. When copyHugeData is true this ID is returned before the row data has finished populating.

post.description:
Copies one or more views from a source workspace to a destination workspace. The two workspaces may belong to the same organization or to different organizations, which makes this a cross-workspace operation unlike Save As View.

The source workspace is the `workspace-id` in the URL and the destination workspace is `destWorkspaceId` in the CONFIG. The destination *organization* is resolved from the headers, and which header carries it depends on the caller:

- An **Account Admin** sends the destination organization in `ZANALYTICS-ORGID` and no second header. This is the default route, and it is why `ZANALYTICS-ORGID` means something different here than in every other API in this module.
- An **Organization Admin** with admin access in several organizations sends their own organization in `ZANALYTICS-ORGID` and the destination in `ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID`. The service then checks that the caller is a member of that destination organization before copying.

Either way, when the destination organization differs from the organization of the source workspace, the copy key of the source workspace must also be sent as `workspaceKey`.

The response maps each source view ID to the ID of the view newly created in the destination workspace.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | The source or the destination workspace was not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL and destWorkspaceId in the CONFIG are valid. |
| 7104 | One or more view IDs in viewIds do not exist. | Verify that every view ID in the array exists and is accessible. |
| 7301 | The user does not have permission. Raised when the user is not an Account Admin or Organization Admin of the destination organization, when the caller is not a member of the organization named in ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID, or when createAsSystemTable is used outside an authorized internal service. | Ensure the user is an Account Admin or Organization Admin of the destination organization and, when ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID is used, a member of that organization. |
| 7319 | One or more view IDs do not belong to the source workspace given in the URL. | Ensure that every view ID in viewIds comes from the workspace given in the workspace-id path parameter. |
| 8058 | The organization ID sent in ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID does not exist. | Provide a valid, existing organization ID in the ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID header. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.create scope. |
| 15007 | Cross-organization copy is not authorized. Raised when the resolved destination organization differs from the organization of the source workspace and workspaceKey is missing or incorrect. | Provide the correct workspaceKey of the source workspace for a cross-organization copy. |

parameters.name: ZANALYTICS-ORGID
parameters.description: ID of an organization, but which one depends on the caller. When ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID is not sent - the Account Admin route - this header carries the destination organization, because the permission check validates the caller's admin rights in the destination. When ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID is sent - the Organization Admin route - this header carries the caller's own source organization instead. Note that this differs from every other API in this module, where the header always names the organization of the workspace in the URL.

parameters.name: ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID
parameters.description: ID of the destination organization. It is meant for an Organization Admin who holds admin access in several organizations and wants to copy into one of them while keeping their own organization in ZANALYTICS-ORGID. When it is sent, it overrides destination resolution and the service validates that the caller is a member of it, failing with error 7301 otherwise and with error 8058 if the organization does not exist. When it is omitted, the destination organization is the one in ZANALYTICS-ORGID.

parameters.name: workspace-id
parameters.description: ID of the source workspace that holds the views to be copied.

sameOrgCopy.description: Copies two listed views into a destination workspace that belongs to the same organization. No workspace key is needed and dependent views are not resolved.

copyWithDependents.description: Copies a table together with every analysis view built on it, and keeps going when an individual view in the expanded set fails to copy.

crossOrgCopy.description: Copies views into a workspace in another organization. The copy key of the source workspace is mandatory here, and the destination organization travels in ZANALYTICS-ORGID for an Account Admin or in ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID for an Organization Admin. The whole operation is rolled back on the first failure.

200.description: OK. The views were copied and each source view ID is mapped to its new destination view ID.

allViewsCopied.description: Every requested view was copied. One entry is returned per view, mapping the source view ID to the newly created destination view ID.

partialCopy.description: With continueOnFailure set to true, only the views that copied successfully are listed. Views that failed are absent from the array and are not reported separately.

noViewsCopied.description: With continueOnFailure set to true and every view failing, HTTP 200 is still returned with an empty views array and no error is raised.

post.description:
Replicates, for a target table, every analysis view - chart, pivot table, summary view and so on - that exists on a reference table in the same workspace. The column bindings in each copied view are remapped automatically to the corresponding columns of the target table.

The target table is the `view-id` in the URL and the reference table is `referenceViewId` in the CONFIG. This is useful when two tables share a compatible column structure and a whole set of reports needs to be reproduced from one on the other.

All generated views are placed into the single folder given as `folderId`.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is valid. |
| 7104 | The target table given as view-id, or the reference table given as referenceViewId, was not found. | Verify that both view IDs exist in the workspace. |
| 7144 | The specified folderId does not exist in this workspace. | Provide a valid, existing folder ID from within the same workspace. |
| 7301 | The user is not authorized to create views in this workspace. | Ensure the user is an Account Admin, Organization Admin, or Workspace Admin. |
| 7319 | One or both view IDs do not belong to the specified workspace. | Ensure that the view-id in the URL and the referenceViewId in the CONFIG both belong to the workspace given in the URL. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.create scope. |

structureOnlyCopy.description: Replicates the reference table's views on the target table with their axis and filter bindings alone. No formula column of either kind is carried over.

allFormulasCopy.description: Replicates the views and carries over both custom formula columns and aggregate formula columns. Use this only when the target table supports the same expressions.

aggFormulaOnly.description: Replicates the views with the summary-level aggregate formulas but leaves the row-level custom formula columns behind.

204.description: No Content. The similar views were created for the target table.

put.description:
Renames an existing view and, optionally, updates its description. It applies to every view type - tables, analysis views, dashboards, query tables and others.

The description is always overwritten. If `viewDesc` is not sent, the existing description is cleared to an empty string, so the current description has to be passed explicitly whenever it should be retained.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7104 | View not found. | Verify that the view-id exists in the specified workspace. |
| 7111 | A view with the given viewName already exists in this workspace. | Choose a unique name for the view. |
| 7301 | The user does not have permission to rename this view. | Ensure the user is a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, Organization Admin, or the view owner. |
| 7319 | The view does not belong to the specified workspace. | Verify that the workspace-id and the view-id are correct and consistent. |
| 7413 | viewName is empty. | Provide a non-empty, valid view name. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.update scope. |

renameOnly.description: Changes the view name alone. Because viewDesc is not sent, the existing description of the view is cleared to an empty string.

renameWithDescription.description: Changes the view name and sets a new description in the same call. This is the form to use whenever the description must survive the rename.

renameDashboard.description: Renames a dashboard. The new name is reflected wherever the dashboard is referenced, without any further update call.

204.description: No Content. The view was renamed.

delete.description:
Deletes a view from a workspace. The delete is a soft delete - the view is moved to the workspace Trash, from where it can be restored within the retention period. It applies to every view type.

If other views depend on the view being deleted - analysis views built on a table, charts embedded in a dashboard, or a query table referencing the table - the call fails unless `deleteDependentViews` is set to `true`, in which case those dependents are deleted alongside it.

**Notes**

> Note:
>
> - This is a soft delete. The view is moved to the workspace Trash and can be brought back with the Restore Trash View API within the retention period, after which it is purged permanently.
> - The CONFIG parameter is optional. When it is omitted, **deleteDependentViews** is taken as false.
> - When **deleteDependentViews** is false and another view depends on this one, the request fails with a dependency error and nothing is deleted. Use the Get View Details API with **withInvolvedMetaInfo** as true to identify the dependents first.
> - When **deleteDependentViews** is true, direct and transitive dependents go with the view in the same operation. A table with 50 analysis views loses all 50, and an analysis view embedded in dashboards takes those dashboards with it.
> - Deleting an individual dashboard tab removes that tab and every view it holds from the parent tabbed dashboard. If it is the last remaining tab, the parent tabbed dashboard itself may be affected.
> - Deleting a tabbed dashboard deletes the parent object, and its constituent tabs count as dependents. Send **deleteDependentViews** as true to remove them in the same call.
> - Deleting a table that acts as a lookup source leaves orphaned lookup columns in the tables that reference it. Send **deleteDependentViews** as true, or remove the lookup relationship first.
> - Every view removed by this call goes to Trash separately and must be restored individually from there.
> - The API returns HTTP 204 No Content with an empty body on success.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7104 | View not found. | Verify that the view-id exists in the specified workspace. |
| 7301 | The user does not have permission to delete this view. Raised when the user is neither a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, Organization Admin, nor the view owner. | Ensure the user holds one of the required roles. |
| 7319 | The view does not belong to the specified workspace. | Verify that the workspace-id and the view-id are correct and consistent. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.delete scope. |

deleteStandalone.description: Deletes a view that nothing else depends on, such as a chart or a dashboard. Sending deleteDependentViews as false is the explicit form of the default behaviour.

deleteWithDependents.description: Deletes a table together with every view that depends on it, direct and transitive. All of them are moved to Trash and have to be restored individually.

204.description: No Content. The view was moved to the workspace Trash.

get.description:
Returns the list of views accessible to the authenticated user within a workspace, together with the folder, creator and last-modifier metadata of each view.

The result can be narrowed by view type, by a keyword matched against the view name, and by the user who created or last modified the view, and it can be paged and sorted. The scope of the list depends on the caller: an admin receives every view in the workspace, while a shared user or group member receives only the views shared with them.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7301 | The user does not have permission to list the views of this workspace. | Ensure the user has at least Read permission on the workspace. |
| 8119 | Invalid value for sortedColumn, which must be 0 to 2, or for sortedOrder, which must be 0 to 1. | Use only the documented integer values for the sort attributes. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.metadata.read scope. |

parameters.name: CONFIG
parameters.description: JSONObject that filters, pages and sorts the view list. As this is a GET request, the value must be stringified and URL encoded before it is sent.

dashboardsAndTables.description: Returns only the dashboards and the base tables of the workspace, ordered by last modified time with the most recently changed view first.

keywordSearchPaged.description: Returns the first ten views whose name contains Revenue, ordered by name ascending. Increase startIndex by noOfResult to walk through the remaining pages.

viewsByUser.description: Returns only the views created or last modified by one user, identified by ZUID, with the newest created view first.

200.description: OK. The list of views accessible to the calling user in the workspace.

adminViewList.description: An admin receives every view in the workspace. The analysis view carries parentViewId pointing at the table it is built on, and sharedBy is empty for admins.

sharedUserList.description: A shared user receives only the views shared explicitly with them, and sharedBy names the user who shared each one.

emptyResult.description: A filter that matches nothing still returns HTTP 200 with an empty views array rather than an error.

get.description:
Returns the metadata of a single view identified by its view ID. The view is resolved globally, so unlike the other APIs in this module no workspace ID is needed in the URL - the workspace is derived from the view itself.

By default only the base attributes are returned. Setting `withInvolvedMetaInfo` to `true` adds extended metadata whose shape depends on the view type: column definitions and a row count for tables and query tables, the tab structure for a tabbed dashboard, and the list of parent views for an analysis view or a regular dashboard. Some of those extended fields are restricted to Workspace Admins.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7104 | View not found. | Verify that the view-id is valid and accessible. |
| 7301 | The user does not have Read Only permission on the view. | Ensure the user has been granted at least Read Only access to the view. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.metadata.read scope. |

parameters.name: ZANALYTICS-ORGID
parameters.description: ID of the organization. It is not required by this API, since the view is resolved globally by its ID, but sending it is harmless and is recommended for consistency with the other APIs.

parameters.name: CONFIG
parameters.description: JSONObject that controls whether extended metadata is returned along with the base view attributes. As this is a GET request, the value must be stringified and URL encoded before it is sent.

baseDetails.description: Returns the base attributes of the view alone. This is the same result as omitting the CONFIG parameter entirely.

extendedDetails.description: Adds the extended metadata for the view type - column definitions and row count for a table or query table, tab structure for a tabbed dashboard, parent views for an analysis view.

200.description: OK. The metadata of the requested view.

baseTableDetails.description: The base attributes of a table, returned when withInvolvedMetaInfo is false or the CONFIG parameter is omitted.

tableWithColumns.description: A table requested with withInvolvedMetaInfo as true. The column definitions are returned to every user with access, while the row count is restricted to Workspace Admins.

tabbedDashboardDetails.description: A tabbed dashboard requested by a Workspace Admin with withInvolvedMetaInfo as true. Each tab lists the views it holds.

involvedViews.viewName: Sales and Profit in each Region

dashboardTabDetails.description: An individual tab requested by its own view ID. parentViewId points at the tabbed dashboard the tab belongs to.

queryTableDetails.description: A query table requested by a Workspace Admin with withInvolvedMetaInfo as true, showing its columns alongside the parent tables the query is built on.

get.description:
Generates and returns the publicly accessible URL of a view. The URL opens directly in a browser without authentication, which allows the view to be shared outside Zoho Analytics.

The generated URL carries the visual customisations sent in the CONFIG - theme, title and description visibility, toolbar, legend position - and can also apply a data filter through `criteria`, so that whoever opens the link sees only the filtered subset.

When the view has been made public with a private key, that key is embedded in the URL path and the link works only for someone who holds it.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7104 | View not found. | Verify that the view-id exists in the specified workspace. |
| 7301 | The user does not have Publish or Make Public permission on the workspace. | Ensure the user is a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, Organization Admin, or has been granted Publish or Make Public permission. |
| 7319 | The view does not belong to the specified workspace. | Verify that the workspace-id and the view-id are correct and consistent. |
| 8060 | The specified domainName does not exist. | Provide a valid custom domain name configured for the workspace. |
| 8061 | The specified domain does not belong to the workspace or the calling user. | Use a domain that is associated with the workspace. |
| 8062 | withCustomDomain is true but no custom domain is configured for this workspace. | Configure a custom domain for the workspace first, or omit withCustomDomain to use the standard domain. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.embed.read scope. |

parameters.name: CONFIG
parameters.description: JSONObject that controls the appearance of the view in the generated URL and, optionally, the data filter applied to it. As this is a GET request, the value must be stringified and URL encoded before it is sent.

themedWithFilter.description: Generates a URL with the green theme and no toolbar or description, showing only the rows that match the criteria when the link is opened.

tableDisplayOptions.description: Generates a URL for a table with the search box, the data type symbols and the column visibility toggle turned on. These three attributes have no effect on other view types.

customDomainUrl.description: Generates the URL on a custom client portal domain configured for the workspace instead of the standard Zoho Analytics domain.

200.description: OK. The generated URL of the view.

publicUrl.description: The standard shareable URL of a view that has no private key configured, carrying only the theme.

filteredUrl.description: A URL carrying the display attributes and the filter criteria, both appended as URL-encoded query parameters.

privateKeyUrl.description: A view made public with a private key returns the key as a segment of the URL path. Opening the link without that segment is denied.

get.description:
Returns every active view that depends on the specified view. A dependent view is one that cannot exist without the source view - a chart built on a table, a pivot table built on a query table, or a query table built on another query table.

The whole transitive chain is resolved, so the result is the complete set of views that would break if the source view were deleted. That makes this API a useful check before calling Delete View.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7104 | View not found. | Verify that the view-id exists in the specified workspace. |
| 7301 | The user is not a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, or Organization Admin. | Ensure the user holds a Workspace Admin or higher role in this workspace. |
| 7319 | The view does not belong to the specified workspace. | Verify that the workspace-id and the view-id are correct and consistent. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.metadata.read scope. |

200.description: OK. The active views that depend on the specified view.

tableDependents.description: A table returns the analysis views built on it together with the dashboard that embeds them. The dashboard appears even though it depends on the table only indirectly.

queryTableDependents.description: A query table returns the child query table built on top of it as well as the analysis views built on either of them.

noDependents.description: A dashboard, or any other view that nothing is built on, returns an empty array with HTTP 200 rather than an error.

get.description:
Returns the views most recently accessed by the authenticated user, ordered with the most recent first.

The API is user-scoped and spans workspaces: views from every workspace and organization the user can reach are returned together in one list, each carrying the workspace it belongs to. No workspace ID is needed in the URL, and the history returned is personal to the token used to make the call.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.metadata.read scope. |

200.description: OK. The views recently accessed by the authenticated user.

crossWorkspaceHistory.description: Views of several types drawn from more than one workspace, ordered by the time the calling user last opened each of them.

sharedUserHistory.description: A shared user sees only the views they currently have access to. A view later unshared from them no longer appears here.

noRecentViews.description: A user who has not opened any view yet receives an empty array with HTTP 200 rather than an error.

post.description:
Runs auto analysis on a single column of a table and creates a focused set of views for it - a category breakdown for a dimension column such as Region, or a trend over time for a date column such as Order Date.

Unlike the full-table Auto Analyse View API, this operation keeps no record of having been run, so there is no re-run guard and no `analyseAgain` attribute. Each call produces a fresh set of views for the column and may be repeated freely, which makes it suited to exploring one column after a data or schema change.

The API works on Tables, Query Tables and Pipeline Tables only, and not every column type is eligible.

**Notes**

> Note:
>
> - This API has no CONFIG parameter. The only inputs are the **workspace-id**, **view-id** and **column-id** path parameters, so no Content-Type header is required.
> - Only Tables, Query Tables and Pipeline Tables can be analysed. Passing any other view type as **view-id** fails with error 7397.
> - Column-level analysis keeps no completion state, so there is no equivalent of the **analyseAgain** guard used by the Auto Analyse View API. Every call runs fresh.
> - Repeated calls on the same column each succeed and accumulate views. Delete the previously generated column views manually if the duplicates are not wanted.
> - Not every column is eligible. Auto-Number, Multi-Line Text, URL and Geometry columns are unsupported, as are hidden columns and system columns such as the row ID. An ineligible column fails with error 8116.
> - A column that has been disabled in a Query Table definition cannot be analysed and fails with error 14037. Enable it in the query table configuration first, or choose another column.
> - A Geo Number latitude or longitude column is eligible only when both are present and visible as a pair. A lone latitude or longitude column cannot be analysed on its own.
> - The views generated are targeted at the selected column - a category breakdown for a dimension column, a time series for a date column - rather than the comprehensive set produced by the Auto Analyse View API.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7104 | View, or table, not found. | Verify that the view-id exists in the specified workspace. |
| 7107 | Column not found in the specified table. | Verify that the column-id belongs to the table identified by the view-id. |
| 7301 | The user does not have Create Report permission on the workspace. | Ensure the user is a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, Organization Admin, or has been granted Create Report permission on this workspace. |
| 7319 | The view does not belong to the specified workspace. | Verify that the workspace-id and the view-id are correct and consistent. |
| 7397 | The view is not a Table, Query Table, or Pipeline Table. | Auto analysis works on base table types only. Pass the ID of a valid table view. |
| 8116 | The selected column type is not supported for auto analysis, such as an Auto-Number, Multi-Line Text, URL or Geometry column, or a hidden or system column. | Choose an eligible column. The unsupported column characteristics are listed in the notes for this API. |
| 14037 | The column is disabled in its Query Table definition and cannot be used for analysis. | Enable the column in the query table configuration, or choose a different column. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.create scope. |

200.description: OK. The views were generated for the column.

reportsGenerated.description: The same body is returned whatever the type of the analysed column. A dimension column and a date column both report success this way, though the views created differ.

post.description:
Runs auto analysis on an entire table. Every column is scanned, the role of each is inferred - dimension or measure, geographic, temporal - and a curated set of views is created directly in the workspace.

The operation tracks its own completion state. Once a table has been analysed successfully it is marked internally as analysed, and a second call is rejected with error 8116 unless `analyseAgain` is set to `true`. That guard exists to stop auto-generated views being duplicated by an accidental repeat call; setting the flag signals deliberate intent, and the previous set of views is then replaced rather than added to.

The API works on Tables, Query Tables and Pipeline Tables only.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7104 | View, or table, not found. | Verify that the view-id exists in the specified workspace. |
| 7301 | The user does not have Create Report permission on the workspace. | Ensure the user is a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, Organization Admin, or has been granted Create Report permission on this workspace. |
| 7319 | The view does not belong to the specified workspace. | Verify that the workspace-id and the view-id are correct and consistent. |
| 7397 | The view is not a Table, Query Table, or Pipeline Table. | Auto analysis works on base table types only. Pass the ID of a valid table view. |
| 8116 | Auto analysis has already been completed for this table and analyseAgain was not set to true. | Send CONFIG with analyseAgain as true to re-run the analysis and replace the previously generated views. |
| 8535 | Invalid or expired OAuth token. | Provide a valid token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.create scope. |

firstAnalysis.description: Runs auto analysis on a table for the first time. Sending analyseAgain as false is the explicit form of the default, and is equivalent to omitting the CONFIG parameter entirely.

reAnalysis.description: Re-runs auto analysis on a table that has already been analysed, for instance after new columns were added or the SQL of a query table was changed. The earlier set of auto-generated views is replaced.

200.description: OK. The views were generated for the table.

reportsGenerated.description: The same body is returned for a first-time run and for a re-run with analyseAgain as true. The difference lies in the request, not the response.

post.description:
Marks the specified view as a favorite for the authenticated user.

The favorite status is a per-user preference - marking a view as a favorite does not change what any other user sees. Once the view is marked, the `isFavorite` field returned by the listing APIs such as Get All Dashboards and Get Shared Dashboards reads `true` for the same user.

The call is idempotent. Marking a view that the user has already marked as a favorite succeeds silently without raising an error.

**Notes**

Before restoring, the service checks whether any parent objects the view depends on - the base table, its columns, formulas, relations and data connectors - are also in the trash. If they are, the restore succeeds only when `withDependents` is set to `true`; otherwise it fails with error 7941. When the parents are already active, or the view is standalone, the restore succeeds either way.

> Note:
>
> - The CONFIG parameter is optional. When it is omitted, **withDependents** is taken as false.
> - Restore fails with error 7941 when the view depends on parent objects that are also in the trash and **withDependents** is false.

> - When restoring several views that were deleted together, restore the parent tables first with **withDependents** as false, then restore the child views. This avoids unintended cascading restores.
> - To restore a DashTab, its parent tabbed dashboard must be active. If the parent dashboard is also in the trash, restore the dashboard first or send **withDependents** as true.
> - If the folder that originally held the view was deleted as well, the view is restored into the workspace root folder. The folder does not need to be restored first.
> - A view listed with **isDisabled** as true cannot be restored under the current plan. Upgrade the plan or delete the view permanently.
> - Error 7929 indicates that the view was already restored, possibly by another user or process. Confirm using the Get Trash Views API.
> - The API returns HTTP 204 No Content with an empty body on success.

| 7929 | The view has already been restored from the trash. | The view is active again. No action is needed. |
| 7941 | The view has parent dependencies that are also in the trash and must be restored together. | Retry the request with withDependents set to true in the CONFIG. |
| 7943 | The requesting user does not have permission to restore this specific trashed view. | Only the original owner of the view or an admin can restore it. |
| 8535 | Invalid OAuth token. | Provide a valid, non-expired token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.create scope. |

standaloneRestore.description: Restores a view whose parent objects are already active, or which has no parents at all. Sending withDependents as false is the explicit form of the default behaviour.

restoreWithDependents.description: Restores the view together with the parent objects it needs - the base table, its columns, formulas, relations and data connectors - that are also in the trash.

204.description: No Content. The view was restored from the trash into the workspace.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes the specified view from the trash. The view, its columns, formulas and relations are removed for good and cannot be recovered.

Before deleting, the service checks whether any child dependent views - reports, pivot tables, summary views or query tables built on this view - are also in the trash. If they are, the delete succeeds only when `withDependents` is set to `true`, in which case the children are permanently deleted along with the view; otherwise it fails with error 7942.

**Error codes**

| Code | Meaning | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7082 | An unexpected error occurred during the permanent delete operation. | Retry the request. If the error persists, contact support. |
| 7103 | Workspace not found. | Verify that the workspace-id in the URL is correct and accessible. |
| 7301 | The user does not have permission to delete this view from the trash. | Ensure the user is a Workspace Admin, Account Admin, Organization Admin, or the original owner of the trashed view. |
| 7929 | The view has already been restored from the trash and is no longer in the trash bin. | The view is active again and cannot be deleted from the trash. |
| 7942 | The view has child dependent views in the trash that must be deleted together. | Retry the request with withDependents set to true in the CONFIG. |
| 8535 | Invalid OAuth token. | Provide a valid, non-expired token with the ZohoAnalytics.modeling.delete scope. |

deleteStandalone.description: Permanently deletes a view that has no child dependent views in the trash, such as an analysis view or a pivot table.

deleteWithDependents.description: Permanently deletes the view together with every child dependent view of it that is also in the trash. This cannot be undone.

204.description: No Content. The view was permanently deleted from the trash.

AutoAnalyseResponse.title: AutoAnalyseResponse
AutoAnalyseResponse.description: Response returned by the Auto Analyse View and Auto Analyse Column APIs.

data.description: Container that holds the outcome of the analysis.

status.description: Message describing the outcome of the analysis, such as Reports generated successfully.

AutoAnalyseViewConfig.title: AutoAnalyseViewConfig
AutoAnalyseViewConfig.description: Configuration that controls whether auto analysis may re-run on a table that has already been analysed.

analyseAgain.description: Controls whether auto analysis may run again on a table that has already been analysed. When true, the views generated by the previous run are discarded and a fresh set is created from the current data and schema, which is what to send after adding columns or importing significantly different data. When false, a table that already carries auto-generated views is rejected with error 8116, guarding against accidental duplication. Sending true on a table that has never been analysed is permitted and simply runs the first-time analysis.

CopiedView.title: CopiedView
CopiedView.description: Mapping between a view in the source workspace and the view newly created for it in the destination workspace.

sourceViewId.description: ID of the view in the source workspace.

destViewId.description: ID of the view newly created in the destination workspace. Use this ID to reference the copy going forward.

CopiedViews.title: CopiedViews
CopiedViews.description: JSONArray holding one entry per view that was copied successfully. Views that failed are absent from the array, and the array is empty when no view was copied.

CopyViewIds.title: CopyViewIds
CopyViewIds.description: JSONArray holding the IDs of the views to be copied. Every ID must belong to the source workspace given in the URL; an ID that does not fails with error 7319, and an ID that does not exist fails with error 7104.

items.description: ID of a view in the source workspace.

CopyViewsConfig.title: CopyViewsConfig
CopyViewsConfig.description: Configuration that controls which views are copied and where they are copied to.

destWorkspaceId.description: ID of the destination workspace into which the views are copied. It must belong to the organization that is finally resolved as the destination - the one in ZANALYTICS-DEST-ORGID when that header is sent, otherwise the one in ZANALYTICS-ORGID.

workspaceKey.description: Copy key of the source workspace, made up of alphanumeric characters and obtained from the source workspace settings. It is required whenever the resolved destination organization differs from the organization of the source workspace, on both the Account Admin and the Organization Admin route, and a cross-organization copy without a matching key fails with error 15007. For a copy within one organization the key is ignored even if it is sent.

copyWithDependentViews.description: Controls whether the views that depend on each listed view are resolved and copied as well. When true, the analysis views built on a table being copied are added to the operation automatically. When false, only the explicitly listed view IDs are copied, and a dependent view left out that references a table which is not being copied may fail or land in a broken state in the destination.

continueOnFailure.description: Controls how a failure on an individual view is handled. When true, a view that fails to copy - because of a name conflict, for example - is skipped and the remaining views continue, returning a partial result. When false, the whole operation is rolled back on the first failure. It takes effect only when copyWithDependentViews is true, because each listed view is otherwise attempted independently.

createAsSystemTable.description: Controls whether the copied tables are marked as system tables in the destination workspace, a special internal classification. It is restricted to specific internal service integrations, and using true outside such a context fails with error 7301. External consumers should omit it or send false.

copyWithData.description: Reserved for future use. The attribute is accepted by the API but is not processed by the copy operation at present - table row data is not transferred across workspaces, only the schema and the view definitions.

CopyViewsResponse.title: CopyViewsResponse
CopyViewsResponse.description: Response returned by the Copy Views API.

data.description: Container that holds the source-to-destination view mapping.

CreateSimilarViewsConfig.title: CreateSimilarViewsConfig
CreateSimilarViewsConfig.description: Configuration that identifies the reference table to replicate views from and the folder the generated views are placed in.

referenceViewId.description: ID of the reference table within the same workspace. Every analysis view built on this table is used as a template. If the reference table has no analysis views, the call succeeds and no view is created.

folderId.description: ID of the folder within the workspace in which all the newly created similar views are placed. There is no default. A folder that does not exist in the workspace fails with error 7144.

copyCustomFormula.description: Controls whether the custom formula columns defined on the reference table's views are copied and mapped onto the target table. When false, the formula column definitions are left out of the copied views. Set it to true only when the target table carries compatible column definitions, since a formula whose expression references a missing column is created in an error state.

copyAggFormula.description: Controls whether the aggregate, or summary-level, formula columns defined on the reference table's views are copied onto the target table's views. When false, the aggregate formulas are left out. The same caution applies as for copyCustomFormula - set it to true only when the target table supports the same aggregate expressions.

CreateTagConfig.title: CreateTagConfig
CreateTagConfig.description: Configuration that defines the tag to be created. Both attributes are mandatory.

name.description: Display name of the tag, 1 to 100 characters. Must be unique within the workspace, otherwise error 8174. The same name may exist in another workspace as an unrelated tag.

colorCode.description: Hex colour of the tag in the form #RRGGBB or #RGB, case-insensitive. Colour keywords, rgb() notation, eight-digit values with an alpha channel and values without the leading # fail with error 8509. The colour is presentation only and need not be unique.

CreateTagResponse.title: CreateTagResponse
CreateTagResponse.description: Response returned by the Create Tag API.

data.description: Container that holds the identifier of the newly created tag.

tagId.description: ID of the newly created tag, returned as a string. The read APIs return the same value as id. Use it as the tag-id path parameter and as a tagIds entry in the association APIs.

DashboardTab.title: DashboardTab
DashboardTab.description: A single tab of a tabbed dashboard, together with the views it holds.

DashboardTabs.title: DashboardTabs
DashboardTabs.description: JSONArray holding the tabs of a tabbed dashboard. Returned only when withInvolvedMetaInfo is true, and restricted to Workspace Admins.

DeleteTrashViewConfig.title: DeleteTrashViewConfig
DeleteTrashViewConfig.description: Configuration that controls how a view is permanently deleted from the trash.

withDependents.description: Controls whether the child dependent views of this view are permanently deleted along with it. When set to true, the view and every child dependent view of it that is also in the trash - dependent reports, formulas and relations - are permanently deleted together. When set to false, the delete fails with error 7942 if any child dependent view is still in the trash. Deletion with dependents is irreversible.

DeleteViewConfig.title: DeleteViewConfig
DeleteViewConfig.description: Configuration that controls how a view with dependents is deleted.

deleteDependentViews.description: Controls whether the views that depend on this one are deleted along with it. When true, the target view and every view that depends on it - direct dependents and dependents of dependents - are deleted in the same operation, which covers the analysis views built on a table, the dashboards holding those views and the query tables referencing the table. When false, the delete fails with a dependency conflict if any other view depends on the target, and nothing is deleted.

DependentView.title: DependentView
DependentView.description: A single active view that depends on the view the request was made for.

viewId.description: Unique identifier of the dependent view.

viewName.description: Display name of the dependent view.

viewTypeId.description: Integer type code of the dependent view. The code 9, for a dashboard tab, never appears here because tabs are not listed as dependents.

viewType.description: Human-readable type label of the dependent view, such as Chart View, Pivot View, Summary View, Query Table or Dashboard. These labels differ from the viewType strings returned by the Get View List API, where the same chart appears as AnalysisView.

DependentViews.title: DependentViews
DependentViews.description: JSONArray holding the active views that depend on the specified view, resolved through the full transitive chain. Empty when nothing depends on it.

GetRecentViewsResponse.description: Response returned by the Get Recent Views API.

GetTaggedViewsConfig.title: GetTaggedViewsConfig
GetTaggedViewsConfig.description: Configuration that pages the list of views carrying the tag. When omitted, every view carrying the tag is returned. No total count or cursor is returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of views to return. When omitted, every view carrying the tag is returned.

offset.description: Number of views to skip before collecting the result. Used together with limit to page through a large association list.

GetTaggedViewsResponse.title: GetTaggedViewsResponse
GetTaggedViewsResponse.description: Response returned by the Get Tagged Views API.

data.description: Container that holds the tagged views.

GetTagsResponse.description: Response returned by the Get Tags List API.

GetViewDependentsResponse.description: Response returned by the Get View Dependents API.

data.description: Container that holds the dependent view list.

GetViewDetailsConfig.title: GetViewDetailsConfig
GetViewDetailsConfig.description: Configuration that controls whether extended metadata is returned with the view details.

withInvolvedMetaInfo.description: Controls whether extended metadata is returned alongside the base view attributes. When true, the additional fields depend on the view type - columns and rowCount for a table, columns, rowCount and involvedViews for a query table, tabs for a tabbed dashboard, and involvedViews for an analysis view, pivot table, summary view or regular dashboard. When false, only the base attributes are returned. rowCount, involvedViews and tabs are restricted to Workspace Admins and are returned as null to other users, while columns is returned to every user with access to the view.

GetViewDetailsResponse.title: GetViewDetailsResponse
GetViewDetailsResponse.description: Response returned by the Get View Details API.

data.description: Container that holds the view metadata.

GetViewListConfig.title: GetViewListConfig
GetViewListConfig.description: Configuration that filters, pages and sorts the view list.

keyword.description: Filters the views by a case-insensitive partial match on the view name. Sending Sales, for example, returns every view whose name contains Sales. When omitted, no name filter is applied.

startIndex.description: Zero-based index of the first record to return, used together with noOfResult to page through a large workspace. When omitted, the result starts at index 0.

noOfResult.description: Maximum number of views to return. When omitted, every matching view is returned.

sortedColumn.description: The column the result is sorted by. A value outside the listed range fails with error 8119.

sortedOrder.description: The direction the result is sorted in. A value outside the listed range fails with error 8119.

criteriaZuid.description: ZUID of a user, restricting the result to the views that user created or last modified. When omitted, the views of every user are returned.

GetViewTagsResponse.title: GetViewTagsResponse
GetViewTagsResponse.description: Response returned by the Get View Tags API.

data.description: Container that holds the tags attached to the view.

GetViewUrlConfig.title: GetViewUrlConfig
GetViewUrlConfig.description: Configuration that controls the appearance of the view in the generated URL and, optionally, the data filter applied to it.

theme.description: Visual theme applied to the view in the generated URL, appended to it as ZDB_THEME_NAME. The standard theme names are blue, bluedark, grey, green, violet, fire, tango and contrast.

includeTitle.description: Controls whether the view title is rendered in the shared page. When false, the title bar is hidden and the view content gains that vertical space.

includeDesc.description: Controls whether the view description is shown below the title in the shared page.

includeToolBar.description: Controls whether the toolbar, which carries the export, share and other action buttons, is shown. When false, the page has a cleaner read-only appearance.

includeSearchBox.description: Controls whether a search box is shown above the data, letting the viewer run keyword searches within it. Applies to tables and tabular views only and is silently ignored for charts, pivot tables and dashboards.

includeDatatypeSymbol.description: Controls whether a data type icon is shown next to each column name, so that the viewer can tell text, number and date columns apart at a glance. Applies to tables and tabular views only.

includeShowHideOption.description: Controls whether a column visibility toggle is shown, letting the viewer show or hide individual columns without edit access to the view. Applies to tables and tabular views only.

legendPosition.description: Placement of the chart legend in the generated URL. Applies to chart, or analysis, views only and is silently ignored for tables, pivot tables and dashboards. When omitted, the position saved in the view's own settings is used.

criteria.description: Zoho Analytics filter criteria applied to the data behind the URL, encoded and appended to it as CRITERIA. Whoever opens the link then sees only the rows that match. The criteria must reference columns that exist in the view. When omitted, all the data is shown.

withCustomDomain.description: Controls whether the URL is generated on the custom client portal domain of the workspace rather than the standard Zoho Analytics domain. It fails with error 8062 when the workspace has no custom domain configured. Prefer domainName when the domain needs to be named explicitly.

domainName.description: Custom domain to use in the generated URL, which takes precedence over withCustomDomain. The domain must be one configured for the workspace; a domain that does not exist fails with error 8060, and one that does not belong to the workspace or the calling user fails with error 8061.

GetViewUrlResponse.title: GetViewUrlResponse
GetViewUrlResponse.description: Response returned by the Get View URL API.

data.description: Container that holds the generated URL.

viewUrl.description: The complete, ready-to-use URL of the view, carrying the visual customisations and the filter criteria as query parameters. For a view made public with a private key, the key appears as a segment of the URL path.

InvolvedView.description: Reference to a parent view or table that the requested view is built on.

viewName.description: Display name of the involved view.

viewType.description: Type of the involved view, such as Table, Chart View or Pivot View.

InvolvedViews.description: JSONArray holding the parent tables or views that the requested view is built on. Returned only when withInvolvedMetaInfo is true, and restricted to Workspace Admins.

RecentView.description: A single view recently accessed by the authenticated user, together with the workspace it belongs to.

workspaceId.description: ID of the workspace that holds this view.

workspaceName.description: Display name of the workspace that holds this view, useful for telling apart views drawn from several workspaces.

viewLastAccessedTime.description: Epoch timestamp in milliseconds at which the calling user last accessed this view, returned as a string.

RecentViews.title: RecentViews
RecentViews.description: JSONArray holding the views recently accessed by the authenticated user across every workspace they can reach, ordered by viewLastAccessedTime descending. Empty when the user has no view history.

RemoveTagFromViewsConfig.title: RemoveTagFromViewsConfig
RemoveTagFromViewsConfig.description: Configuration that names the views the tag is detached from, or requests that the tag be detached from every view in the workspace. Exactly one of the two mechanisms applies - either send viewIds, or set dissociateAll to true. An empty or absent viewIds with dissociateAll off fails with error 8201.

dissociateAll.description: When true, the tag is detached from every view in the workspace and viewIds is ignored. The reach is workspace-wide, including views the caller may not otherwise interact with, and no count is returned. Required unless viewIds is sent.

RemoveTagsFromViewConfig.title: RemoveTagsFromViewConfig
RemoveTagsFromViewConfig.description: Configuration that names the tags to detach from the view, or requests that every tag be detached from it. Exactly one of the two mechanisms applies - either send tagIds, or set dissociateAll to true. An empty or absent tagIds with dissociateAll off fails with error 8202.

dissociateAll.description: When true, every tag is detached from this one view and tagIds is ignored. The reach is limited to the view in the request URI. Required unless tagIds is sent.

RenameViewConfig.title: RenameViewConfig
RenameViewConfig.description: Configuration that carries the new name, and optionally the new description, of the view.

viewName.description: The new display name for the view. It must be non-empty, otherwise the request fails with error 7413, and unique within the workspace, otherwise it fails with error 7111. The name follows the standard view name validation rules for length and allowed characters.

viewDesc.description: The new description for the view. It is always overwritten - when this attribute is omitted the existing description is cleared to an empty string rather than preserved, so the current description must be passed explicitly to retain it.

RestoreTrashViewConfig.title: RestoreTrashViewConfig
RestoreTrashViewConfig.description: Configuration that controls how a view is restored from the trash.

withDependents.description: Controls whether the parent objects the view depends on are restored along with it. When set to true, the view is restored together with the parent objects that are also in the trash and are required for it to function - the base table, its columns, formulas, relations and data connectors. When set to false, the restore fails with error 7941 if any required parent object is still in the trash. Only the ancestors the view needs are restored; sibling views that depend on the same parent are not.

SaveAsViewConfig.title: SaveAsViewConfig
SaveAsViewConfig.description: Configuration that controls how an existing view is duplicated within the same workspace.

viewName.description: The display name for the newly created view. It must be unique within the workspace; a name that is already in use fails with error 7111. The length follows the standard view name validation rules of the workspace.

viewDesc.description: A short description for the new view. When omitted, the new view is created with an empty description.

copyWithData.description: Controls whether the row data of the source table is copied along with its structure. When true, the new table is a full copy including all existing rows. When false, only the schema is copied - columns, data types, lookup references and formula definitions - and the new table holds no rows. Applies to tables only and is ignored for analysis views.

copyWithLookup.description: Controls whether the lookup, or join, relationships defined on the source table are replicated on the copy. When true, the copied lookups point at the same referenced tables, so the new table joins the same relational model. When false, the lookup definitions are dropped and the new table is standalone. Applies to tables only and is ignored for analysis views.

copyHugeData.description: Controls whether the data copy is processed asynchronously in the background. When true, the API returns the new viewId immediately while the rows continue to populate, which avoids a request timeout on a large table. When false, the call waits until the data copy is complete before returning. It takes effect only when copyWithData is true, and applies to tables only.

folderId.description: ID of the folder within the workspace in which the new view is placed. The folder must exist in the same workspace as the source view; otherwise the request fails with error 7144. When omitted, the new view is placed in the root-level unorganised area of the workspace.

TaggedView.title: TaggedView
TaggedView.description: A view that carries the tag.

TaggedViews.title: TaggedViews
TaggedViews.description: JSONArray holding the views that carry the tag and that the calling user is entitled to see. Empty when the tag labels nothing visible to the caller.

Tags.description: JSONArray of tags. Empty when there are none. For the Get View Tags API it holds at most 10 entries.

TrashView.title: TrashView
TrashView.description: Details of a single view that is currently in the trash of the workspace.

viewName.description: Display name the view carried at the time it was deleted.

deletedTime.description: Epoch timestamp in milliseconds at which the view was deleted, returned as a string.

isDisabled.description: Indicates that the view cannot be restored under the current plan, typically a Live Connect report on a plan that no longer supports Live Connect. Returned only when it is true.

tabParentName.description: Display name of the parent tabbed dashboard. Returned only when viewType is DashTab.

tabPosition.description: Position index of this tab within the parent tabbed dashboard. Returned only when viewType is DashTab.

TrashViews.title: TrashViews
TrashViews.description: JSONArray holding the views that are currently in the trash of the workspace. Empty when the trash holds nothing visible to the calling user.

UpdateTagConfig.title: UpdateTagConfig
UpdateTagConfig.description: Configuration that carries the new name and/or colour of the tag. At least one of the two must be present, otherwise error 8182. The attribute that is omitted keeps its stored value.

colorCode.description: Hex colour of the tag in the form #RRGGBB or #RGB, case-insensitive. Colour keywords, rgb() notation, eight-digit values with an alpha channel and values without the leading # fail with error 8509. The colour is presentation only and need not be unique. ViewColumn.title: ViewColumn

dataType.description: Internal data type identifier of the column, such as PLAIN, DATE_AS_DATE or CURRENCY.

dataTypeId.description: Numeric ID of the data type.

isHidden.description: Indicates whether the column is hidden in the view.

decimalSeparator.description: Character used as the decimal separator. Returned only for numeric columns.

ViewColumns.title: ViewColumns
